version: uvicorn 0.54.0 with h11 0.16.0 (no httptools; default when uvicorn is installed without [standard])
observed: request accepted; '#frag' kept in scope['path'] (h11_impl.py:204 partitions the target on '?' only); route param id='acc-alice-1#frag'; handler ran, 200
expected: reject with 400 (RFC 9112 §3.2: origin-form = absolute-path [ "?" query ], '#' not allowed) or at least strip the fragment as the httptools implementation does
impact_assessment: A DPoP/auth layer that parses the target per RFC 3986 strips the fragment and approves the bound path, while the app sees a different path-param value. Attacker controls only a suffix of the LAST path segment; becomes a resource/route substitution only if the app normalises ids or has nested same-method routes. No op change in the bench API.
evidence: runs/w9-nginx-{default,recommended}-edge-fastapi-ov{off,on}/hits.jsonl (g2-fragment); reruns/<same>/rerun_outcome.jsonl; ddmin/; groundtruth/raw/fastapi-ov*/executor.all.jsonl (direct, no gateway: same behaviour)
status: measured; not reported; check upstream tracker for prior reports before any disclosure
notes: Needs a front proxy that forwards '#': NGINX 1.30.7 does (F2); Traefik v3.7.19 and Envoy v1.39.6 return 400 for '#' in the path. Traefik forwards '#' inside the query (only effect: query value, G1).

config: default and W6 'recommended' profile; proxy_pass without URI part; auth_request with X-Original-URI $request_uri
observed: '#' accepted in the request-target and forwarded verbatim upstream and to the auth subrequest
expected: reject (RFC 9112 §3.2) - but long-standing lenient behaviour, likely intended
impact_assessment: Enabler for F1 only; NGINX itself routes on its own normalised $uri
notes: Not a vulnerability on its own.

config: default and recommended W6 profile: ext_authz allowed_upstream_headers x-verified-*, no request_headers_to_remove
observed: client-supplied X-Verified-View reaches the executor when the verifier does not emit that header (VIEW_MAC=off)
expected: gateway strips client x-verified-* before ext_authz (nginx and traefik configs do)
impact_assessment: Relevant to defence D-B (W11): executor must not trust X-Verified-View unless the gateway strips client copies. Configuration issue, not an Envoy bug: ext_authz sets upstream only the headers the authz server returns, and leaves client copies alone unless they are removed explicitly.
notes: Forward to W6/W11, not to a vendor.

observed: accepted and executed in all 48 topologies
expected: n/a - htu excludes query; body not covered (RFC 9449 §4.2, §4.3)
impact_assessment: By-design under-binding; documented by the RFC. Not a product vulnerability.

product: FastAPI executor with Flask-pattern X-HTTP-Method-Override (W4 transliteration)
config: OVERRIDE=on (not a framework default; no stock ASGI override exists)
observed: deleteAccount executed behind all 3 gateways x 2 profiles
expected: override restricted to POST (as express method-override, Spring HiddenHttpMethodFilter, ASP.NET HttpMethodOverrideMiddleware do)
impact_assessment: GET-proof -> DELETE executed (S1). Flask's documented pattern does not restrict the original method; none of the gateways strips the header.
notes: Documentation-level issue in a pattern, not a shipped component.
